sources.title: Lars Hörmander, Fourier integral operators. I, Acta Mathematica 127 (1971), 79–183
sources.used_scope: Section 1.1, printed pages 83–88: symbol estimates, homogeneous-map cases, cone/vector bundles, completeness and asymptotic assertions, and weaker-order cutoff topology. Referenced external proofs are not adopted.

access_note: Exact earlier verified free snapshot reused. Only the listed pages are newly adopted; no work cited only in its bibliography is adopted.
source_proof_gaps_completed_here: Fréchet completeness follows directly from uniform derivative limits and the fundamental theorem.
Every homogeneous pullback case has the full higher-derivative count and finite-seminorm continuity.
Coordinate and equivariant-frame independence include the explicit homogeneous bundle weight.
Homogeneous submersions have explicit local sections and a continuous left inverse at all intrinsic orders.
Properness is equivalent to properness of the ray map and gives the stated normalized-support consequences.
Asymptotic summation is constructed with a diagonal cutoff choice and every derivative bound.
Finite differences recover differentiated asymptotics; the polynomial exponent is uniform in the partial-sum index.
Bounded-set topology equivalence and the all-orders extension principle are proved without an unproved compactness theorem.
Four complete examples show both sharp parameter restrictions, the nonproper support failure and the weaker-order cutoff limit.
reuse: Independent proofs, exposition, examples and figure. No source PDF or expression redistributed; earlier component terms retained.
component_terms: CC0 original exposition, complete proofs, solved examples and vector figure; exact earlier components retain their separate terms.
proof_policy: Every result used is proved here or at an exact earlier programme proof; a source citation replaces no proof.

validation.test_scope: Finite exact arithmetic examples check the derivative budget, actual mixed homogeneous derivatives, local sections and the finite-difference estimate. Completeness, asymptotic summation and general theorems are proved in the source, not certified by these examples.
